recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-5313 follow-up is needed unless the work group separately wants broader modernization of registry or standards-status wording outside this ballot comment.
issue_request: FHIR-5313 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification ballot comment asking HL7 to clarify that widely adopted extensions should not automatically be promoted into core resource elements, while still allowing migration with widespread implementer endorsement and allowing draft extensions to move before normative finalization.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in August 2015 in source/defining-extensions.html by SVN-derived commits 9ed8870a0e (#5313: Updated wording applied) and 2bca95adc1c (#5313: fix build). Later blame on the current lines shows only spelling corrections for the applied wording.
additional_context: Current source/defining-extensions.html:278-281 contains the wide-endorsement exception, forced-migration rationale, draft movement rule, and normative stability rule. The page remains part of the active extensibility documentation surface, with ExtensionDefinition mapped to the FHIR work group in source/fhir.ini and links from source/extensibility.html. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later directly relevant decision or conflicting community discussion.
reconciliation: No source edit was made because the current source already conveys the approved resolution. The nearby statement that broadly adopted extensions may be elevated into the base resource structure is compatible with FHIR-5313's exception for migrations endorsed by the implementer community.
